title: RAE2822 grid-to-solver dependency workflow
overview: Generate an RAE2822 mesh artifact first, then bind that exact output into a dependent Roe-SA CFD case. The workflow demonstrates explicit producer-consumer relationships instead of relying on shared working-directory state.
principle: A dependency workflow is a directed execution graph. A consumer may run only after its direct producer succeeds and the declared artifact exists. Artifact paths are relative to the producer case, while the consumer receives an explicit source-case root and a case-relative input setting. Independent steps may proceed without being blocked by an unrelated failed branch.
architecture: The workflow definition is parsed by the Qt-independent workflow plan builder. build_case_graph_plan validates case IDs, dependencies, artifact producers, direct producer-consumer edges, and safe relative paths, then emits dependency-respecting WorkflowPlanStep records. run_case_graph stages each case into an isolated run root by default, rewrites declared consumer parameter settings, verifies producer outputs before launching consumers, blocks unsuccessful dependencies, and checks declared outputs after a successful callback. The Workbench presents the declared graph and links to the existing plan and runner tests; it does not execute CFD during catalog loading.

verification.scope: Versioned example definition; catalog validation checks that the typed graph payload matches this file but does not execute it.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_workflow_plan.py; validates the real example through build_case_graph_plan.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_workflow_graph_runner.py; checks isolated staging, producer artifact binding, consumer parameter rewrite, and source-case preservation.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_workflow_graph_runner.py; checks dependency failure blocking while an independent branch still runs.
tools/oneflow_gui/test_workflow_graph_runner.py; checks missing declared producer output prevents consumer execution.

proves: The example declares one mesh producer and one Roe-SA consumer with a direct dependency edge.
The producer and consumer refer to the same stable artifact ID and relative output path.
The consumer binds the producer artifact through gridFileName in script/cfd.txt.
Existing plan and runner tests cover dependency ordering, isolated staging, artifact availability, failure blocking, and source-case preservation.
does_not_prove: The RAE2822 example has been executed as a complete CFD workflow in the current revision.
The mesh conversion or Roe-SA solver produces scientifically correct results.
A successful callback alone proves the physical validity of the generated mesh or CFD solution.
Every possible workflow graph, artifact type, cancellation race, or filesystem failure is covered.
